requirement:
Sections use `section`, named from whitespace-normalized heading text. ATX and
setext headings are supported. Content before the first heading can form an
anonymous section. Section nesting follows heading levels; other outline items
appear beneath their nearest enclosing container. Selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test source only and did not request any implementation source. The marked tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.sections`.

- **`section` kind and whitespace-normalized names**
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` expects `# Head  *one*` to become `section[Head%20*one*]`.
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` expects `Heading   words` to become `section[Heading%20words]`.
  - `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` expects a two-line setext heading to become `section[Títle%20two]`.
  - The same test also checks that `===` inside a fenced code block does not create a heading.
- **ATX and setext headings**
  - ATX headings are covered in `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` and `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`.
  - Setext `===` is covered in `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble`.
  - Setext `---` is covered in `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`, in `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` and in `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans`.
  - The last of these also puts setext headings inside a directive, a block quote and a list. It asserts their spans, name spans and section text.
- **Anonymous preamble**
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` expects a `section@…` node for the text before the first heading.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` also expects one and checks its text is `préface`.
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` covers a preamble after front matter.
- **Nesting follows heading levels**
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` has a level skip (`# Main` then `### Deep`).
  - It has same-level siblings and duplicates (`section[Same]#1` and `#2`).
  - It has a level-1 setext heading that closes the earlier sections (`# End`).
  - It has a `## Peer` that returns to a sibling under `End` after a deeper heading.
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` and `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` check simple parent and child nesting.
- **Other items beneath the nearest enclosing container**
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` asserts the full parent-index structure. Paragraphs and blocks sit under the section, and nested paragraphs and blocks sit under their enclosing block. It also checks that each selector resolves back to its node and that line ranges match.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` expects a block selector of the form `section[End]/section[Level%20two]/block@…`.
- **Selectors follow the outline selector grammar**
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` percent-encodes `/`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@` and `%`. It also covers `#N` duplicate disambiguation and selecting by the resulting selectors.
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` checks that each generated selector resolves to its own node.

The assertions check exact selector lists and span text, not just execution, so a wrong name, nesting or span would fail them. The requirement says anonymous content "can" form a section, which is a MAY, so it needs no test. The requirement does not name other heading forms, such as closing ATX hashes, so I did not treat their absence as a gap.
